JUDGMENT
Both these appeals arise out of the impugned judgment and award dated 08.11.2016 passed in M.V.C. No.2/2015 by the Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Yellapur, Sitting at Haliyal.

sentences.text:
2. Heard the learned counsel for the claimant and the learned counsel appearing for the North-West Karnataka Road Transport Corporation, ('NWKRTC').
3.

The material on record discloses that the claimant-Kamalakar filed the aforesaid claim petition seeking compensation towards the injuries sustained by him in a road traffic accident that occurred on 01.09.2014 when he was traveling in the NWKRTC Bus bearing registration No.KA-31/F-1299 from Joida, and the said bus met with an accident on account of rash and negligent driving by the driver of the said NWKRTC bus.

The said claim petition having been opposed by the Corporation,
the Tribunal proceeded to pass the impugned judgment NC: 2023:KHC-D:10792-DB and award allowing the claim petition in part, thereby directing payment of compensation in a sum of Rs.14,67,480/- together with interest at the rate of 7% per annum from the date of claim petition till the date of payment excluding Rs.75,000/- already awarded in favour of the claimant.

4. The appeal - M.F.A. No.103105/2017 is preferred by the claimant seeking enhancement of compensation, while M.F.A. No.102761/2018 is preferred by the NWKRTC aggrieved only by the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal.

5. A perusal of the grounds urged in the respective memorandums of appeals and the material on record will indicate that the occurrence of the accident and the liability of the NWKRTC to pay compensation are not in dispute and both the appeals are restricted to the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal.

While it is the specific contention of the NKWKRTC that the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal is NC: 2023:KHC-D:10792-DB excessive and exorbitant, the claimant contends that the compensation awarded is inadequate and meager and the same deserves to be enhanced by this Court.
In this regard, the learned counsel for the claimant submits that the claimant suffered from grievous injuries for which he is undergoing treatment.

It is also submitted that, apart from the evidence already produced by the claimants before the Tribunal,
the claimant has custody and possession of additional evidence which he seeks to produce for the purpose of seeking enhancement of compensation.
The said submission made by the learned counsel for the claimant is placed on record.
6. As stated supra, the only issue that requires adjudication in the present appeals is with regard to the quantum of compensation payable in favour of the claimant.
